metadata.neutral_citation: LAM MEI LAN v. LEUNG YUK AND OTHERS [1979] HKCFI 7; HCA 676/1979
metadata.case_name: LAM MEI LAN v. LEUNG YUK AND OTHERS

injuries.description: deep laceration on the left occiput of the head with the skull bone exposed
source: (a) deep laceration on the left occiput of the head with the skull bone exposed;
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of head

injuries.description: mild abnormality in her brain resulting from injury to her head
source: As a result of the injury to her head, the young plaintiff is suffering from a mild abnormality in her brain; her speech is still not as fluent as other children of her age; she suffers from a moderate grade of memory impairment and has great difficulty in memorising new information supplied purely on verbal data;

injuries.description: superficial abrasion of her left shoulder and both of her knees, her left ankle and left forearm
injuries.body_part: left shoulder; both knees; left ankle; left forearm
source: (b) superficial abrasion of her left shoulder and both of her knees, her left ankle and left forearm;

manifestations.description: speech is still not as fluent as other children of her age
moderate grade of memory impairment; great difficulty in memorising new information supplied purely on verbal data
abstract thinking is poor due to the injury to her brain
intelligence compares unfavourably with normal children at the age of 4
will develop an inferiority complex which will result in emotional crises

treatments_received: taken to Chai Wan Clinic (immediately after PLB returned)
examined at Casualty Department of Tang Shiu Kin Hospital (10:13 a.m. on day of accident)
rehabilitation treatment at Sandy Bay for one month

losses.description: memory impairment, poor abstract thinking and reduced intelligence compared with normal children

losses.category: Loss of ability to pursue education
losses.description: will not be able to complete her secondary education; academically limited (best up to Form 3 or 4)
loss of prospects of marriage because of her condition
limited in the type and scope of jobs open to her; can do repetitive factory work, domestic service or cook; will never be able to do work requiring substantial use of brain
will feel lonely and depressed, particularly when her parents do not understand her condition

comparable_cases.case_name: Leung Chi Ming v. So Ki Yim
comparable_cases.injury_description: permanent disabilities of the plaintiff in that case were somewhat more serious than those of the plaintiff in this case

comparable_cases.case_name: Lau Kai Tai v. Tsang Chor Chau
comparable_cases.injury_description: case discussed as distinguishable; plaintiff there lost chances of certain careers
